final_response:
The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is defined as the ratio of **signal power** to **noise power**. Since power is proportional to voltage squared (for the same impedance):

$$\text{SNR} = \frac{P_s}{P_n} = \left(\frac{V_s}{V_n}\right)^2$$

Given that the peak signal voltage is 20 times the peak noise voltage:

$$\frac{V_s}{V_n} = 20 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \text{SNR} = 20^2 = \boxed{400}$$

Converting to decibels:

$$\mathrm{SNR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 10\log_{10}(\text{SNR}) = 10\log_{10}(400) = 20\log_{10}(20) \approx 26.0206\ \mathrm{dB}$$

To 3 significant figures:

$$\boxed{\mathrm{SNR} = 400,\quad \mathrm{SNR}_{\mathrm{dB}} = 26.0\ \mathrm{dB}}$$
